previous_disclosures.section: Note 4 - Stock-Based Compensation > Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
previous_disclosures.summary: The NVIDIA Corporation 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan allows participating employees to purchase shares using up to 15% of their withheld earnings at a discounted price of 85% of the lower of fair market values at commencement or purchase dates. As of January 29, 2023, 230 million shares were reserved for future issuance under this plan.

current_disclosures.section: Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation > Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
current_disclosures.summary: Starting in March 2025, employees participating in the 2012 Plan may have up to 25% of their earnings withheld to purchase common stock, an increase from the previous 15% limit, though the Board retains discretion to decrease this percentage.

current_disclosures.section: Note 3 - Stock-Based Compensation > Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan
current_disclosures.summary: The 2012 Plan features offering periods of approximately 24 months, divided into four six-month purchase periods, with purchase prices set at 85% of the lower of the fair market value at the commencement date or on each purchase date.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 filing explicitly states that the withholding limit for the ESPP increased from 15% to 25% starting in March 2025. This is a concrete, quantitative change to the plan mechanics that directly alters the terms for participating employees, representing a material modification to the company's equity compensation structure.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Increase in ESPP earnings withholding limit from 15% to 25%

comparisons.peer_summary: Under the 2017 Plan, eligible employees can withhold up to 15% of earnings to purchase shares at 85% of the lower of fair market value on the first or last day of a six-month offering period commencing in May and November.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose the core mechanics of their respective Employee Stock Purchase Plans (ESPP), specifically the withholding limit and the discount structure. Both companies allow employees to withhold up to 15% of earnings to purchase shares at 85% of the fair market value. However, they differ in the timing of the price comparison: NVIDIA bases the purchase price on the lower of the fair market value on the commencement date or *each* purchase date within a 24-month offering period divided into four six-month intervals, whereas AMD bases its price on the lower of the fair market value on the first or last business day of a six-month offering period.

sentences.text: Employees who participate in the 2012 Plan may have up to 15% of their earnings withheld to purchase shares of common stock.

The price of common stock purchased under our 2012 Plan will be equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value of the common stock on the commencement date of each offering period or the fair market value of the common stock on each purchase date within the offering.
Each offering period is about 24 months, divided into four purchase periods of six months.

Under the 2017 Plan, eligible employees who participate in an offering period may have up to 15% of their eligible earnings withheld, up to certain limitations, to purchase shares of common stock at 85% of the lower of the fair market value on the first or the last business day of the six-month offering period.
The offering periods commence in May and November each year.
